new password works for IMAP and SMTP straight away. Ends the mailbox's other mail sessions and

get.description:
Anyone else sees the rows of the domains they have a role on, without account and server
history (`admin.*`, `maildir.*`, `user.*` except `user.invited`). `domain` follows the console's
domain rules (422 when malformed); one that is unknown or outside the user's domains gives an
empty page. `actor` is a user id, `mailbox:` plus a mailbox's address, `cli` or `system`
(GET /audit-log/actors lists them). `from` (inclusive) and `to` (exclusive) are ISO 8601
date-times with an offset. `before_id` anchors the pages: send the first page's newest id with
every later page, so rows written in between don't shift them.
get.summary: What happened on the user's domains, newest first (ties broken by id); a server admin sees every row

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: A domain name in ASCII (punycode) or Unicode, any case: 422 when malformed, an empty page when unknown or not yours.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description: A user id, `mailbox:` plus a mailbox's address, `cli` or `system` (GET /audit-log/actors lists them).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive: an ISO 8601 date-time with an offset (`Z` or `±hh:mm`); seconds and fractions optional.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Exclusive: an ISO 8601 date-time with an offset, as `from`.

parameters.name: before_id
parameters.description:
The paging anchor: only rows with an id up to this one. Send the first page's newest id
with every later page, so rows written meanwhile don't shift the pages; drop it when the
filters change.

parameters.name: per_page
parameters.description: How many rows a page holds: 10 by default, at most 200. `limit` is accepted too, as on the other lists.

get.description:
Each check: `status` (`ok`, `warn`, `fail`, or `info` for MTA-STS and autoconfig), `found` (the
records seen), `expected` (the value looked for, where there is one), `hint_key` (what to tell
the user, translated by the SPA) and, when something should be published, `publish`: the record's
`name`, `type`, `value` (the text to copy) and `zone` (a zone-file line, long TXT split into
255-byte strings). `dkim` also lists the console's pending and active keys in `selectors`, each
with whether DNS shows its record.
get.summary:
The latest stored check. A domain never checked gets one queued on this first read and answers
`result: null` with `checking: true` until it has run; `checking` is also true while a recheck
waits in the queue

patch.description:
A name alone needs no step-up; an email, role or status does (423 `step_up_required`, checked
after validation: an invalid body answers 422 first). A field that keeps its value changes
nothing. A new email tells the old address and revokes pending invitations to it. Making someone
a server admin removes their grants; changing the role or deactivating signs them out everywhere. 409
`cannot_change_self` when you demote or deactivate yourself; 409 `last_server_admin` when it
would leave no active server admin.
patch.summary: Changes a user's name, email, server-admin role or status; at least one of them

403.description: Not allowed (`forbidden`), or two-factor authentication must be set up first (`two_factor_required`)

409.description: Conflict: `cannot_change_self` (not on yourself) or `last_server_admin` (it would leave no active server admin)

423.description: Step-up required (`step_up_required`) to change an `email`, `is_server_admin` or `status` (a `name` alone needs none): confirm the password or code with POST /auth/confirm-password, then retry. Checked after validation, so an invalid body answers 422 first

delete.description:
Their grants and sessions go with them; invitations they sent, and pending invitations to their
email, stop working. 409
`cannot_change_self` for yourself; 409 `last_server_admin` for the last active server admin.

when the email already has that access or a pending invitation to it; 409 `user_deactivated`

The invitation is sent in the name of whoever resends it. An accepted or revoked invitation, or
one whose domain is gone, answers 409 `invitation_closed`; one that creating would now refuse
answers the same 409.

actor_kind.description:
Who acted, as a stable value the console words in its own language: `you` is the requester,
`mailbox` a mailbox owner in the portal.

actor_name.description: The user's name, or the mailbox's address; an English label for the other kinds.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: PUT /portal/password: the mailbox's current password and the new one, which follows the mailbox rules.

current_password.description: The mailbox's password now; the mail server checks it.

password.description: 12 or more characters, at most 72 bytes, strength 3 or more, and not in a known breach when that check is on.

ChangePasswordRequest.title: ChangePasswordRequest

status.description: A deactivated user keeps the grant but has no role until reactivated.

granted_by_name.description: Who gave the grant (their email when their name is empty); null when unknown or that user is gone

used_bytes.description: Sum of the domain's mailbox usage; null when no usage was read yet

quota_bytes_allocated.description: Sum of the mailboxes' quotas, a default quota counted as `quota_default_bytes`

max_mailboxes.description: At most this many mailboxes; null is unlimited

max_quota_bytes_total.description: At most this many quota bytes allocated in total; null is unlimited

people_count.description: How many people have a grant on the domain; server admins have every domain and are not counted, even with a grant left from before

people.description: The first three of those people's names (the email when a name is empty), by name

role.description: The requester's role on this domain: `admin` (a server admin), `manager` or `viewer`.

domain.description: The domain's ASCII name; null for a server-admin invitation
The domain's ASCII name; null for a server-admin invitation

domain_unicode.description: The domain's unicode name; null for a server-admin invitation

invited_by_name.description: Who sent it (their email when their name is empty); null when that user is gone

state.description: `valid`, `expired`, or `revoked` when its domain is gone or its inviter can no longer send it

mailbox.description: `true` signs in to the mailbox only: the console account is not tried, so an address whose console and mail passwords are the same reaches its portal. Absent or `false`, the console account is tried first.

usage_checked_at.description: ISO 8601, or null when usage was never read

invited_by_name.description: Who sent it (their email when their name is empty); null when that user is gone

state.description: `valid`, `expired`, or `revoked` when its inviter can no longer share the domain

code.description: Stable snake_case identifier the client switches on.

PutPortalForwardingRequest.description: PUT /portal/forwarding: where the owner's mailbox forwards to, and whether it keeps a copy.

targets.description: At most 10 distinct addresses (`+` allowed; at most 50 entries in all), never the mailbox itself; an empty list turns forwarding off.

keep_copy.description: Keep a copy in the mailbox as well; ignored when `targets` is empty.

PutPortalForwardingRequest.title: PutPortalForwardingRequest

SendWelcomeRequest.description:
The welcome email's recipient and language (POST /domains/{domain}/mailboxes/{mailbox}/welcome).
`to` is one bare address: the endpoint sends mail to an address a manager types, so it must never
carry a display name, a list or a header.

to.description: One plain email address, at most 254 characters: no display name, list or header characters. Sent as typed, trimmed, with the domain lowercased.

SendWelcomeRequest.title: SendWelcomeRequest

SetupRequest.description: A setup link or a reset link: the token, its email and the new password.
SetupRequest.title: SetupRequest

StoreAliasRequest.description: POST /portal/aliases: a new address on the owner's own domain that delivers to their mailbox.

local.description: The part before `@`; the domain is always the mailbox's own. Letters, numbers, dots, hyphens and underscores, no `+`.

StoreAliasRequest.title: StoreAliasRequest

StoreDomainInvitationRequest.description: An invitation to a role on the domain in the route (POST /domains/{domain}/access/invitations).

note.description: A note to the invitee, printed in the mail as plain text.

locale.description: The language of the mail, and of the invitee's console if they are new.

name.description: What to call the invitee in the mail; a new invitee chooses their own name when accepting.

StoreDomainInvitationRequest.title: StoreDomainInvitationRequest

StoreUserGrantRequest.description: A grant from the Users screen (POST /users/{user}/grants): a role on the domain named in the body.
StoreUserGrantRequest.title: StoreUserGrantRequest

StoreUserInvitationRequest.description:
An invitation from the Users screen (POST /users/invitations): to be a server admin, or to a role on
a domain named in the body.

note.description: A note to the invitee, printed in the mail as plain text.

locale.description: The language of the mail, and of the invitee's console if they are new.

name.description: What to call the invitee in the mail; a new invitee chooses their own name when accepting.

domain.description: The domain (ASCII or unicode) for a `manager` or `viewer`; leave it out for a `server_admin`.

StoreUserInvitationRequest.title: StoreUserInvitationRequest

UpdateUserRequest.description:
A change to a console user from the Users screen (PATCH /users/{user}); at least one field. A name
alone needs no step-up; an email, role or status does.

name.description: The name shown in the console, 1–100 characters.

email.description: The address they sign in with; stored lowercased, and no other user may have it.

is_server_admin.description: Make them a server admin (their grants are removed: they have every domain) or take the role away.

status.description: `deactivated` signs them out everywhere and keeps them out until `active` again.

UpdateUserRequest.title: UpdateUserRequest
